- A transaction changing both to unequal values fails atomically.

```sql
BEGIN;
SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '100ms';
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '2s';

CREATE FUNCTION sync_user_name() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  old_changed boolean;
  new_changed boolean;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
    IF NEW.display_name IS NOT NULL
       AND NEW.preferred_name IS NOT NULL
       AND NEW.display_name IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.preferred_name
    THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'conflicting user names' USING ERRCODE = '23514';
    END IF;

    NEW.display_name := COALESCE(NEW.display_name, NEW.preferred_name);
    NEW.preferred_name := NEW.display_name;
  ELSE
    old_changed := NEW.display_name IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.display_name;
    new_changed := NEW.preferred_name IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.preferred_name;

    IF old_changed AND new_changed THEN
      IF NEW.display_name IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.preferred_name THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'conflicting user names' USING ERRCODE = '23514';
      END IF;
    ELSIF old_changed THEN
      NEW.preferred_name := NEW.display_name;
    ELSIF new_changed THEN
      NEW.display_name := NEW.preferred_name;
    ELSE
      NEW.preferred_name := COALESCE(
        NEW.preferred_name, NEW.display_name
      );
    END IF;
  END IF;

  IF NEW.display_name IS NULL OR NEW.preferred_name IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'user name must not be null' USING ERRCODE = '23502';
  END IF;

  IF NEW.display_name IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.preferred_name THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'user names diverged' USING ERRCODE = '23514';
  END IF;

  RETURN NEW;
END $$;

CREATE TRIGGER users_sync_user_name
BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON users
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_user_name();

COMMIT;
```

A `BEFORE` row trigger can modify the row being stored; the synchronization happens within the original write transaction. [PostgreSQL trigger functions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/plpgsql-trigger.html)

- [ ] **Step 2: Add this bounded operation.**

```sql
CREATE TABLE user_name_migration_progress (
  run text PRIMARY KEY CHECK (run IN ('fill', 'audit')),
  ceiling bigint,
  last_id bigint,
  scanned bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  changed bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  bad_rows bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  done boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false
);

CREATE FUNCTION user_name_batch(p_run text)
RETURNS user_name_migration_progress
LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  progress user_name_migration_progress%ROWTYPE;
  ids bigint[];
  changed_count bigint := 0;
  bad_count bigint := 0;
BEGIN
  IF p_run NOT IN ('fill', 'audit') OR p_run IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'run must be fill or audit';
  END IF;

  INSERT INTO user_name_migration_progress (run, ceiling)
  SELECT p_run, max(id) FROM users
  ON CONFLICT (run) DO NOTHING;

  SELECT * INTO STRICT progress
  FROM user_name_migration_progress
  WHERE run = p_run
  FOR UPDATE;

  IF progress.done THEN
    RETURN progress;
  END IF;

  SELECT array_agg(id ORDER BY id) INTO ids
  FROM (
    SELECT id
    FROM users
    WHERE (progress.last_id IS NULL OR id > progress.last_id)
      AND id <= progress.ceiling
    ORDER BY id
    LIMIT 1000
    FOR UPDATE
  ) AS batch;

  IF ids IS NULL THEN
    UPDATE user_name_migration_progress
    SET done = true
    WHERE run = p_run
    RETURNING * INTO progress;
    RETURN progress;
  END IF;

  IF p_run = 'fill' THEN
    UPDATE users
    SET preferred_name = display_name
    WHERE id = ANY(ids)
      AND preferred_name IS NULL;

    GET DIAGNOSTICS changed_count = ROW_COUNT;
  END IF;

  SELECT count(*) INTO bad_count
  FROM users
  WHERE id = ANY(ids)
    AND (
      preferred_name IS NULL
      OR preferred_name IS DISTINCT FROM display_name
    );

  UPDATE user_name_migration_progress
  SET last_id = ids[array_length(ids, 1)],
      scanned = scanned + array_length(ids, 1),
      changed = changed + changed_count,
      bad_rows = bad_rows + bad_count
  WHERE run = p_run
  RETURNING * INTO progress;

  RETURN progress;
END $$;
```

The cursor and data changes commit together. One worker is sufficient; the progress-row lock serializes accidental duplicates. Do not use `SKIP LOCKED` with this advancing cursor, because skipped rows could be lost behind it.

    ELSIF NEW.preferred_name IS NULL THEN

  job text PRIMARY KEY CHECK (job = 'users'),
  upper_id bigint,
  last_id bigint,
  scanned bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  changed bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  done boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false

SELECT 'users', max(id) FROM public.users
ON CONFLICT (job) DO NOTHING;

CREATE FUNCTION public.backfill_preferred_name_batch()
RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
DECLARE
  p public.preferred_name_backfill%ROWTYPE;
  batch_last bigint;
  batch_scanned bigint;
  batch_changed bigint;
BEGIN
  SELECT * INTO STRICT p
  FROM public.preferred_name_backfill
  WHERE job = 'users'
  FOR UPDATE;

  IF p.done THEN
    RETURN true;
  END IF;

  WITH batch AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM public.users
    WHERE (p.last_id IS NULL OR id > p.last_id)
      AND id <= p.upper_id
    ORDER BY id
    LIMIT 1000
    FOR UPDATE
  ),
  changed AS (
    UPDATE public.users AS u
    SET preferred_name = u.display_name
    FROM batch
    WHERE u.id = batch.id
      AND u.preferred_name IS NULL
    RETURNING u.id
  )
  SELECT max(id), count(*), (SELECT count(*) FROM changed)
  INTO batch_last, batch_scanned, batch_changed
  FROM batch;

  UPDATE public.preferred_name_backfill
  SET last_id = COALESCE(batch_last, last_id),
      scanned = scanned + batch_scanned,
      changed = changed + batch_changed,
      done = (batch_scanned = 0)
  WHERE job = 'users';

  RETURN batch_scanned = 0;
END;
$$;

WHERE name = 'user-name'
FOR UPDATE;

WITH batch AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT u.id
  FROM users u
  JOIN user_name_backfill_progress p ON p.name = 'user-name'
